storylines.title: Galakrond and the Five Proto-Dragons
storylines.summary: Galakrond's predation draws Tyr and five proto-dragons into a struggle that precedes the dragonflights' rise.
storylines.opening: Before the dragonflights had their charge, a hunger threatened the proto-dragons of ancient Azeroth. Tyr's answer depended on five who were not yet Aspects.

chapters.title: Galakrond's hunger
chapters.body: Galakrond’s hunger threatened the proto-dragons of ancient Azeroth. Those who lived beneath that danger could no longer ignore what he had become.

chapters.title: Tyr seeks allies
chapters.body: Tyr turned toward five proto-dragons. They had not yet received the charge of the Aspects, but the struggle would draw their lives together.

chapters.title: Five against one
chapters.body: Tyr and the five confronted Galakrond. The full measure of each part in that struggle remains to be recovered in this unfinished telling.

chapters.title: A charge for the future
chapters.body: After the danger passed, Tyr argued that the five should be empowered. Their victory became a beginning for the dragonflights’ greater duty.

storylines.reviewNote: The official overview is a strong lead; verify detailed motives, battle actions, and northern geography against the original story before promotion. Editorial chapter research tasks retained here: Establish what Galakrond became and why the other proto-dragons could not ignore him. Review the first-party history alongside the original story for the precise origin of his change. Trace Tyr's approach to the five proto-dragons and the different reasons they joined the fight. Their later titles should not be projected backward onto this moment. Follow the confrontation with Galakrond and identify each participant's contribution from primary narrative evidence before writing a finished battle sequence. Examine why Tyr argued for the five to be empowered after the danger passed, and where the story of the Aspects begins rather than ends.

storylines.title: Hero of the Mag'har: Garrosh, Geyah, and Thrall's Return
storylines.summary: Garrosh's shame leads the seeker from Garadar to Oshu'gun, Shattrath, and Auchindoun. The ancestors' danger brings a message to Thrall, whose return and account of Grom's sacrifice change the name Garrosh can bear.
storylines.opening: Beneath Nagrand’s floating islands, the Mag’har endure a history their young Hellscream cannot yet forgive. The ancestors’ unrest carries a stranger toward Geyah’s lost family, and a memory returns to Garadar that Garrosh has never heard.

chapters.title: A burden in Garadar
chapters.body:
Garadar endured beneath Nagrand’s bright sky, a home held together without the strength of the greater Horde around it. At its center stood Garrosh Hellscream, burdened by his father’s name. He remembered Grom through the corruption that had claimed him and feared the same rage within himself. Greatmother Geyah waited with an older memory. Before Garrosh could imagine a future, the weight of that past had to be heard.

Geyah welcomed the seeker as a guest of her people. Materials gathered across Outland were prepared into a potion, opening the way toward the ancestors who still walked Nagrand’s green places. Beyond the village waited Mother Kashur. Garrosh’s grief had drawn the visitor to Garadar; now the Greatmother’s counsel led toward a memory older than his sorrow.

At the Ancestral Grounds, weathered stones and a spring marked a place of listening. Mother Kashur received the seeker there. The ancestors were restless, and their meaning could not be made simple by Geyah’s preparation alone. Kashur asked that the old sites be visited and the spirits’ words brought back. The valley’s quiet held a question the living had yet to understand.

At Sunspring Post, the Laughing Skull ruins, Garadar and the Bleeding Hollow ruins, restless spirits spoke of a call from the south. Their broken words pointed toward Oshu’gun, the pale mountain that had long watched over Nagrand. Scattered unease had found a destination. Mother Kashur sent the seeker onward, toward the place drawing the ancestors beyond their familiar grounds.

chapters.title: The voices beneath the Light
chapters.body:
Oshu’gun rose among Nagrand’s grass and water like a fragment of another world. Beneath its pale mass, the ancestors’ call grew stronger. The mountain was sacred to the Mag’har, yet within its silence waited a presence whose light was failing. The search that had begun with restless whispers now reached the being toward which those lost souls were drawn.

K’ure said that its energies had ebbed over centuries, leaving a Void that consumed nearby souls. Generations of orc ancestors had been drawn into that vortex. The naaru also spoke of the Legion harnessing it to bring void minions into its ranks. Part of the cycle might still be answered. From Oshu’gun, K’ure sent the seeker toward A’dal in Shattrath.

A’dal heard K’ure’s account and answered cautiously. The ancestors’ suffering could not be lifted by a word of Light alone. Another naaru was bound to the question, and the way led toward Auchindoun. Shattrath offered direction without an easy promise of healing. Beneath Terokkar’s ruined halls, another witness might reveal what could still be done for those drawn into darkness.

In the Auchenai Crypts, D’ore explained that the cycle could not simply be stopped: without the Void, the Light could not exist. The spirits threatened by corruption had to be released before darkness consumed them. Beneath blue-grey stone, listening gave way to a difficult duty. The seeker carried a mirror through the crypts, seeking those whose change had already begun.

The Soul Mirror revealed darkened spirits among the ancient orc ancestors. The seeker defeated those already changing, before the Void could take them fully. When the work was done, Mother Kashur received the news at the Ancestral Grounds. The dead had not been restored to life. They had been given a chance to rest beyond the force that called them south.

chapters.title: A message to the Warchief
chapters.body:
Mother Kashur gave thanks for the ancestors released from the darkening cycle and sent the news back to Garadar. Geyah spoke of a people who had endured and might yet know more seasons. Then her concern turned toward Garrosh. He had heard of the seeker’s service; perhaps its meaning could reach him where the Greatmother’s comfort had not.

Geyah asked the seeker to tell Garrosh that the work had been done for him and his people. He could find little comfort in it. The clan might survive another winter, but he could not imagine a future beyond it. His family’s name remained a shame he wished to lay down, and the fear of his father’s corruption still shadowed his own worth.

Garrosh sent word to Geyah that he believed himself unfit to lead. He feared the old corruption might damn the orcs again. In the exchange that followed, Geyah learned that the Horde’s Warchief was Thrall, son of her lost child Durotan. She could not travel to him herself. The seeker would carry an urgent message: his blood still lived upon Draenor.

In Orgrimmar, the seeker delivered Geyah’s message. Thrall answered with astonishment: he had a grandmother, and she lived. Grom’s legacy remained upon the broken world as well. The summons reached beyond war or duty. Thrall would return to Nagrand to meet the family left behind when his parents had crossed the Dark Portal.

chapters.title: A memory returned
chapters.body:
At Garadar, Geyah met the grandson she had feared lost. Thrall also brought Garrosh a memory from the Third War. At Demon Fall Canyon, Grom had stood against Mannoroth and died striking the blow that broke the demon’s hold over the orcs. The corruption and its cost were not erased. Yet the father’s last choice had been hidden beneath the son’s shame.

The memory faded, leaving Garrosh in Garadar with a changed understanding of his name. Grom had broken the demon’s hold at the cost of his life. Garrosh could now call himself son of Grom and chieftain of the Mag’har with pride. Thrall honored the bond he had shared with Grom, then returned to Geyah. The Greatmother received the final news of service to her people.

storylines.title: Karazhan: The Master’s Key and Nightbane
storylines.summary: Alturus’s investigation leads Khadgar to restore a key divided across Outland. A separate Violet Eye search for Medivh’s Journal uncovers a memory of Arcanagos and a ritual that raises Nightbane.
storylines.opening: A tower in Deadwind Pass has sealed itself away, and the Violet Eye’s reading finds a faint demonic echo. The road to reopen Karazhan crosses Outland; the later search for Medivh’s Journal begins a separate inquiry into what the tower remembers.

chapters.title: Restore the Master’s Key
chapters.body:
Below Karazhan, Archmage Alturus watched a tower whose doors had closed against the world. The Violet Eye sought answers among arcane disturbances and restless dead. Beneath the tower and around its grounds, the investigation began along separate paths. An old place had withdrawn into silence, leaving those outside to discover what troubled it and what had become of the people within.

Alturus gave the seeker a Violet Scrying Crystal to read the underground waters of the Master’s Cellar. The result troubled him. Where arcane currents should have flowed, he found a vast energy vacuum and only a faint demonic echo. The cellar had yielded a warning without naming the presence behind it. Above, Karazhan remained closed.

Alturus’s report reached Archmage Cedric in Dalaran’s old crater. Cedric knew the tower had sealed itself, and that the Violet Eye had lost contact with agents inside. The strange reading deepened that silence. He pointed toward Khadgar, Medivh’s former apprentice, now in Shattrath. Someone who remembered the tower’s master might know how its door could be opened.

In Shattrath, Khadgar received the report and recognized a familiar difficulty. Karazhan could not simply be forced open. The Master’s Key had once held that power, and he knew its history. He agreed to help restore it. The way back to the old tower would first pass through Outland’s changed strongholds, seeking what he had left there in another time.

While stranded in Outland, Khadgar had divided his key into three fragments and hidden them in enchanted containers. Their resting places had seemed safe then. The broken world had changed since, and each refuge now bore other dangers. To restore the key, the seeker would have to recover its pieces from places no longer sheltered as their keeper remembered them.

One fragment waited in the Shadow Labyrinth, among passages occupied by the Shadow Council. Khadgar had once trusted that hiding place. Its recovery brought a part of the key out of his memory and into the seeker’s hands. Yet Karazhan’s door remained beyond reach. Elsewhere in Outland, two more fragments lay within strongholds changed by time and occupation.

Another container was recovered in the Steamvault beneath Coilfang Reservoir. Khadgar had hidden it under Serpent Lake before the place bore that name. He suspected the naga’s great drain had carried it into the reservoir. Whatever course the waters had given it, the fragment was found. A changed landscape had yielded another part of the old key.

The last fragment lay in the Arcatraz, a prison within Tempest Keep. Khadgar had hidden it when the naaru held the fortress. Now Kael’thas’s forces had turned the vessel into a place of confinement. From a refuge made dangerous, the seeker recovered the final piece. All three could return to the man who had divided them.

Khadgar restored the key, but it still required Medivh’s consent. Through time, the seeker entered the Black Morass at the Opening of the Dark Portal. Medivh recognized the key as Khadgar’s, though he had not yet given it to his apprentice. Within that remembered past, the restored object received the permission its keeper could not grant for himself.

The key returned to Khadgar in Shattrath. A way into Karazhan now existed. Across changed strongholds and a memory of the past, the seeker had restored the means of entry. Yet an open door could not explain the tower’s silence or the fate of its investigators. Those questions remained with the Violet Eye, waiting beyond the threshold.

chapters.title: The Journal and its Memory
chapters.body:
Within Karazhan, another Violet Eye inquiry sought Medivh’s Journal. Alturus’s earlier agents had not returned; Wravien was the last named seeker. The tower linked this search to the work that had opened its door, but the lost book carried a burden of its own. Among halls rich with knowledge, the investigators hoped to recover a memory of the Guardian himself.

In the Guardian’s Library, Wravien struggled to remember his commission. He directed the seeker to Gradav, whose own work held him fast; Gradav pointed onward to Kamsis. Each offered part of the way, yet none could simply lead the search to its end. The library’s abundance had become an obstacle, and the lost investigators remained caught within their confusion and fixation.

Kamsis directed the seeker toward the Shade of Aran, Medivh’s father. When the shade was overcome, the Journal was recovered. A search for a lost book had reached the chance to witness what its pages preserved. Within Karazhan’s guarded knowledge waited one of Medivh’s own memories, bearing a danger older than the Violet Eye’s present inquiry.

On the Master’s Terrace, the Journal opened upon an older meeting. Arcanagos, a blue dragon, warned Medivh that a dark power sought to use him and urged him to leave. Medivh refused. Magic burned through the dragon from within, and Arcanagos fled aflame. The memory closed upon a terrible act whose remains might still carry part of its meaning.

chapters.title: From Charred Bone to Nightbane
chapters.body:
Alturus wondered whether Medivh had woven some of his essence into the magic that defeated Arcanagos. Perhaps a trace endured in the dragon’s bones. The seeker searched the mountains south of Karazhan and recovered a charred fragment. It was a beginning for the archmage’s inquiry, carrying the possibility of an answer without yet proving what the old magic had left behind.

The bone was sent to Kalynna Lathred in Area 52. Once of the Kirin Tor, she now pursued studies her old order forbade. Alturus called the fragment’s essence lifeless, like Arcanagos himself. Kalynna believed she could help, but asked a price. The Violet Eye’s question had reached a scholar whose boundaries differed from those of the order she had left.

Kalynna demanded two books before completing the favor. Nethekurse held the Tome of Dusk in the Shattered Halls; Darkweaver Syth held the Book of Forgotten Names in Sethekk Halls. Separate journeys brought the volumes within reach. The bargain joined forbidden study to the search for Medivh’s lingering essence, preparing the means to call forth what remained of the dragon.

On the Master’s Terrace, Kalynna’s materials were set alight within a Blackened Urn. The released energy raised Arcanagos’s charred remains as Nightbane. The adventurer defeated him and carried his essence to Alturus. The old memory had yielded a sample, but no full explanation of the Guardian’s power. Above Karazhan, the inquiry ended with an answer still waiting to be understood.

storylines.reviewNote: Complete 18-scene illustrated research story with transcript-matched AI narration, source and claim records, dedicated TBC-area art, distinct principal cast, and pivotal key, journal, bone and urn illustrations. The Master’s Key and Nightbane quest chains are separate and joined editorially at Karazhan; historical travel through the Black Morass and journal memories are explicitly labeled. Target evidence: The Burning Crusade original 2.0.3–2.4.3 quest era, before Wrath-era changes; current accessible references include Blizzard’s TBC Classic overview and secondary reproductions. Original-client/build and exact quest-dialogue capture, chronology, Atiesh scene/model comparison, area-resemblance review, source approval, and narration audition remain open. No Legion Return to Karazhan or later character outcomes are included.

storylines.title: The Missing Diplomat: From Stormwind to Alcaz
storylines.summary: A quiet inquiry reveals Stormwind’s missing king. A later search among a wreck and Alcaz’s marshes deepens the mystery without naming the powerful patron behind it.
storylines.opening: A sealed letter leaves Stormwind Keep and passes through trusted hands. From Duskwood’s farms to the Wetlands harbor and Theramore, the search finds a suspect while the king remains absent. Another inquiry opens among wreckage and the rune-marked pools of Alcaz.

chapters.title: A quiet commission
chapters.body:
At the Cathedral of Light, Thomas asked for an adventurer who could keep a matter private. Bishop DeLavey waited within Stormwind Keep. The request sounded small, yet carried a greater burden: someone within the kingdom had chosen discretion before disclosure. Among the city’s familiar streets, a quiet inquiry began without the public alarm its hidden purpose might have raised.

A diplomat sent to Theramore had never reached Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Bishop DeLavey spoke of an absence not yet commonly known. The king’s agents were searching, but the bishop set his own contacts in motion. A sealed letter went first to Jorgen, a fisherman in the Valley of Heroes. The search had a destination, though no culprit.

Jorgen recognized the bishop’s seal and reluctantly accepted the duty. He wrote to Elling Trias, asking that the confidence placed in him remain intact. From a church office through a fisherman, trust carried the inquiry toward a man who traded in information. No weapon had been drawn. The search advanced through people who knew how to keep a name quiet.

Elling Trias sent the search toward Watcher Backus in Duskwood. Unusual Defias activity offered a lead without yet explaining the Brotherhood’s part in the disappearance. Stormwind’s pale walls gave way to wooded country, where old farms stood beneath fog. Each handoff narrowed the inquiry while leaving its purpose uncertain, carrying the bishop’s confidence into another keeper’s hands.

Backus remembered unusual Defias activity around Addle’s Stead. A search among the dark fields yielded a docket from a chest. He recognized the papers as authentic, but the matter had passed beyond local watchwork. The evidence returned to Elling. Among Duskwood’s secluded farms, the search had recovered writing whose wider meaning waited upon someone who knew the names it carried.

Elling found Dashel Stonefist’s name in the docket. A resident of Stormwind’s Old Town had become the next lead. From papers hidden beneath Duskwood’s canopy, the inquiry returned to familiar streets and guarded reputations. The danger had not passed. Its next door lay within the city, where Elling’s knowledge could turn a written trace into someone who might answer.

chapters.title: A docket in Duskwood
chapters.body:
Dashel admitted that an earlier plan had failed and named Tapoke “Slim” Jahn in another. The search turned north toward Menethil Harbor. From the woods, the trail reached the Wetlands’ cold coast and an inn where Slim might remain unnoticed. A failed operation had left a loose end, carrying the inquiry toward a man who knew more of the vanished voyage.

At the Menethil inn, Slim learned that Elling’s inquiry had reached him. He tried to escape, and a brief struggle ended with his capture. Amid the damp harbor’s crowded rooms and docks, a quiet search had met a suspect who could no longer keep his distance. The questions that had passed through sealed letters could now be put to the man himself.

chapters.title: The missing king
chapters.body:
Slim gave up the name at the center of the search. The missing diplomat was Varian Wrynn, Stormwind’s king. Hendel, he said, had been meant to board the royal ship. The trail now bore the weight of a kingdom’s absence. Yet naming the king and an intended accomplice had not brought Varian home, or revealed what had become of his voyage.

The harbor inquiry pointed toward Commander Samaul in Theramore. Kul Tiras marines travelled from there to Menethil on leave, and Elling’s name could earn the commander’s confidence. From the damp northern docks, the search crossed the sea toward Dustwallow’s fortified port. A military posting offered the next lead, while the vanished king’s own passage remained unknown.

Commander Samaul hesitated before trusting a stranger. Then he named Hendel’s last post: Sentry Point, the first tower beyond Theramore. The outpost watched marsh and shore between the city and the uncertain coast. One soldier now stood at the center of the inquiry, though the commander could not settle what he knew of the plan Slim had described.

At Sentry Point, Archmage Tervosh said Jaina knew of the inquiry and had directed him to help. Hendel was west of the tower, watching Theramore’s scouts return from their search for Brackenwall. The marsh had yielded the soldier’s position. Beyond the watchtower, the investigator approached a man already named in the plan surrounding Varian’s ship.

Hendel resisted, and nearby guards joined the struggle. The adventurer subdued him; Tervosh and Jaina arrived to take him into custody. The search had found a participant whose name was tied to Varian’s ship. It had not found the king. Across the marsh coast, the central disappearance remained unresolved, and the captive still held questions the investigation could not yet answer.

Jaina gave the adventurer her signet ring in thanks. Hendel was held for questioning, but Varian remained absent. The search had passed through Stormwind, Duskwood, the Wetlands and the marsh coast, carrying a quiet appeal into a royal mystery. Its discoveries had reached Theramore without recovering the missing king, and the full purpose behind his disappearance remained beyond their knowledge.

chapters.title: Cargo beneath the marsh
chapters.body:
Another report brought the Defias into view along the Dreadmurk Shore. Lieutenant Aden spoke of survivors near a shipwreck and sent the investigator to Captain Wymor at Sentry Point. A new inquiry began among scattered timbers and coastal waters. If the wreck belonged to the Brotherhood, its cargo might explain what had drawn them so far from their usual ground.

Wymor’s scouts had seen red-bandana Defias near the wreck, far from their Stormwind dealings. On a nearby island, Garn Mathers held an order to protect the cargo at any cost, with payment promised for success and silence. The patron remained unnamed. Wymor sent the writing to Renn McGill, a salvage diver already searching the shore.

Renn confirmed that Defias divers worked among the wreckage. The orders gave him reason to search before they could recover its hidden burden. Broken timbers stretched toward Alcaz through dangerous naga-held waters. Diving gear and tools had to be recovered and repaired. Beneath the waterline, the lost cargo became a trail the investigator could physically follow.

From the broken ship, salvaged strongboxes brought coins, jewelry and letters to the surface. Among the remnants, Renn found enchanted iron manacles. The cargo had included more than valuables: someone had been bound aboard. The cold restraints changed the search, drawing the wreck’s hidden burden nearer the old question of Varian’s disappearance without yet revealing whom they had held.

Renn urged that the manacles be brought to Jaina at once. They showed that a prisoner had been restrained, but could not name that person or reveal their fate. Above the marsh and sea, Theramore’s pale walls sheltered the weighing of another clue. The vanished voyage now stood beside evidence drawn from the wreck, while the greater design remained hidden.

chapters.title: The island and the patron
chapters.body:
Jaina judged Renn’s suspicion about Alcaz worth examining. A large force would overstrain Theramore’s defenses, so she arranged a flight with Cassa Crimsonwing, an apprentice gryphon handler. Knowledge had to come before another commitment of troops. From above the marsh, the island could be observed while its defenders and their purposes remained unknown.

The gryphon passed above Alcaz’s wet, broken ground. Below lay a rune circle, black dragons, naga, hydras and human figures among the marsh pools. The island was crowded with danger. From above, the observer could see their presence without knowing what ties bound them, or what purpose had gathered them upon that uncertain shore.

Jaina believed Defias hedge magic could not explain Alcaz’s rune circle. The island’s inhabitants raised questions she could not settle. Yet she suspected a powerful ally high within the Alliance and tied the plan to Varian’s disappearance. The inquiry had reached beyond the Brotherhood’s own means, leaving a greater patron unnamed behind the missing king’s fate.

Jaina’s findings reached Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. He took the report seriously and planned renewed action against the Defias until the king returned. Lady Katrana Prestor urged him elsewhere, dismissing the charge as speculation. Within Stormwind Keep, the island’s unanswered questions met a divided response. Bolvar asked that Jaina receive his thanks, while the patron she suspected remained unnamed.

The messenger returned to Jaina with Bolvar’s answer. The manacles had revealed a prisoner’s passage; Alcaz had yielded a rune circle and a troubling gathering. Jaina believed a powerful Alliance patron stood behind the Defias. Yet the patron remained unnamed and Varian remained missing. The search ended with thanks and suspicion, carrying its unanswered royal absence back to Theramore.

storylines.reviewNote: Complete 24-scene illustrated research story with source-linked event, claim and citation records; separate Classic and patch 2.3 boundaries; original interpretive character and location art; Stormwind, Duskwood, Wetlands, Theramore, Dreadmurk and Alcaz scenes; and transcript-matched voice-over. StoryTour placement after the Outland Cipher is editorial because this story’s final playable segment was added in patch 2.3; the original Classic chain remains an earlier subperiod. At the story boundary Varian remains missing and the patron is unnamed. Do not conflate either chain with The Great Masquerade, the later Proof of Treachery, comics, Varian’s rescue, or an Onyxia plot. Human source review, original-client comparison, game-area resemblance review and audio audition remain open. Content remains research and never implies exact dates, routes, or co-presence.

storylines.title: Netherwing: Rescue, Disguise, and Liberation
storylines.summary: A kindness to the Netherwing becomes a rescue, an oath and a dangerous disguise. Within the Dragonmaw’s camp, trust carries the seeker toward exposure and an unexpected escape.
storylines.opening: In the violet fields of Shadowmoon Valley, a stranger is asked to help a troubled flight. Beyond the first rescue waits a larger risk: to wear the enemy’s face long enough to learn how far its power reaches.

chapters.title: The captive flight
chapters.body:
Beneath Shadowmoon’s violet sky, Mordenai asked a stranger for kindness. The Netherwing drakes had been disturbed and would not easily trust an offered hand. Prey from the Rocknail hunt was brought to feed them. Before the flight could believe in an ally, someone had to answer an immediate need. Among dark stone and green light, the campaign began with care.

When that first kindness was answered, Mordenai pointed toward Neltharaku. The drake crossed the air above the fields, beyond roads and gates. The seeker found him beneath Shadowmoon’s broken horizon. From the feeding of wary creatures, the journey rose toward one who could speak of the flight’s suffering and the power that held its kin.

Neltharaku spoke of the Dragonmaw forcing Netherwing drakes into service. His people lived beneath another clan’s hand. He asked the seeker to trouble the fortress while he prepared a way to reach those still bound. The kindness offered among the fields had become a call to act, carrying the stranger toward a captivity that reached beyond one drake’s grief.

At Dragonmaw Fortress, the seeker struck the clan’s operation to draw attention away while Neltharaku prepared. The fortress did not fall. A narrow opening had been bought within hostile ground, and the flight’s plan still had to find its means. Beneath the captors’ walls, disturbance offered time for a hope that could not yet free those held inside.

Neltharaku’s plan led to Netherwing Ledge. Amid the Dragonmaw presence, Nethervine crystals were gathered from the broken island. The drake would prepare their power for the work ahead. What had been taken from contested ground could become a means of release, carrying the search from a brief disturbance toward the bonds that held his kin.

Neltharaku gave the crystals power to reach the enslaved drakes’ bonds. At the fortress, the seeker used them to free Netherwing who turned against their captors. Within the clan’s own camp, its forced servants became opponents. Other captives still remained, but those released could now fight beside the stranger whose first help had been offered without a blade.

Neltharaku’s mate Karynaku remained captive high at the fortress. She could speak, though her chains sapped her strength. Zuluhed the Whacked held the key. The larger captivity had narrowed to one drake whose voice could still guide her rescuers. Beyond the freedom already won, the flight’s hope now rested upon reaching the chieftain and opening the restraint he kept.

The seeker confronted Zuluhed, defeated him and recovered Karynaku’s key. Her chains opened. The fortress still sheltered the Dragonmaw’s wider operation, but the drake was free of the restraint that had drained her strength. The way led back toward the fields, carrying an answer to Neltharaku’s plea for the mate who had remained beyond his reach.

Karynaku offered to return the seeker to Mordenai. The Netherwing recognized an ally in the stranger who had fed their kin, troubled the fortress and broken her chains. Trust had been earned within a valley still dangerous to the flight. The first rescue now stood behind a wider promise: to help those whose homeland remained beneath the Dragonmaw’s hand.

chapters.title: Service beneath a borrowed face
chapters.body:
Mordenai called the new ally back with a greater plea. The Netherwing had lost their lands, and their children had been taken into slavery or worse. He asked for an oath to help reclaim their home and guard the flight. The first rescue had opened a wider duty. The seeker now accepted a place within the struggle against the Dragonmaw’s power.

Netherwing magic cloaked the seeker as a Dragonmaw fel orc. With Illidari service papers prepared for Mor’ghor, the disguised ally entered the base camp. Mordenai warned that some sentries could see through the borrowed appearance. The papers were accepted, and the seeker joined the clan’s workers, carrying the flight’s oath beneath orders that concealed its purpose.

Within the camp, Yarzill the Merc revealed himself as a friend to the hidden ally. The goblin’s presence offered a contact among workers who believed the new recruit served the clan. The oath no longer rested upon one disguise alone. A companion stood inside the operation, carrying a purpose the Dragonmaw had not recognized.

Another search among the Netherwing Mines uncovered plans attributed to Murkblood workers. An overseer spoke of revolt against the Dragonmaw and said the clan supplied Illidan’s forces while selling other goods. He suspected outside buyers, even the Black Dragonflight, but could name none with certainty. Beneath the ledge’s labor, another people sought release from the same captors.

Work within the ledge brought the disguised ally deeper into Dragonmaw confidence. At last, Varkule sent the seeker to Mor’ghor. The leader announced a first Highlord and promised that Illidan himself would come to perform the promotion. What had begun as a concealed oath to the Netherwing now approached the gaze of the master whose servants believed the impostor their own.

chapters.title: The Highlord exposed
chapters.body:
Illidan appeared before the gathered camp and saw through the disguise. His anger struck Mor’ghor, then turned toward the seeker. The impostor was to be killed. Mor’ghor answered with threats of vengeance. The promised promotion had become a sentence, and the borrowed face that won entry offered no shelter once its truth was known.

Before Mor’ghor could carry out the threat, Yarzill intervened. The goblin’s disguise fell away, revealing a Netherwing drake. He bore the adventurer out of danger and flew to Shattrath. The camp’s concealment had failed, but its hidden ally preserved the seeker’s life. Beyond Shadowmoon, the rescued stranger could carry the flight’s struggle to those waiting in the city.

In Shattrath’s Lower City, Barthamus received the survivor and heard that the Dragonmaw operation had been exposed. The Netherwing offered companionship in return for the aid they had received. A drake could join the adventurer’s road. The flight’s dangers had not all ended, yet the stranger who first answered a need among Shadowmoon’s fields no longer had to travel alone.
