storylines.title: Quel’Delar: The Broken Blade Restored
storylines.summary: A broken blade carries a kingdom’s sacrifice into a search for restoration. Rival heirs, the darkness of Icecrown and the Sunwell’s light shape what the living may inherit.
storylines.opening: A battered hilt survives beneath the northern cold. Before Quel’Delar can be whole again, its seekers must learn whose hope it once carried and what darkness has entered the steel.

chapters.title: The battered hilt
chapters.body:
From the dangers of the Frozen Halls came a battered hilt, the remnant of a blade whose history had not ended with its breaking. At Quel’Delar’s Rest, the Silver Covenant and Sunreavers took up the question it carried. Before the sword could be made whole, its surviving fragment had drawn rival heirs toward an inheritance neither could leave forgotten.

Caladis Brightspear received seekers of the Silver Covenant; Myralion Sunblaze received those of the Sunreavers. Their allegiances opened different roads through Dalaran. Old kinship between high elves and blood elves could not settle who should hold the blade. Above the city’s violet heights, the hope of restoration stood beside a rivalry over the memory it would carry.

At Wyrmrest Temple, Krasus lent the seekers a history of the ancient blade. Kalecgos questioned whether mortals should command such power; the dragons knew the grief of a mighty weapon turned against them. Alexstrasza permitted the search to continue. Beneath the red-bronze shrine, the hilt’s past began to emerge as both a promise and a warning.

In Dalaran, Caladis and Myralion each directed the search among their own people. Both sought the old blade’s restoration, yet their purposes did not make them one council. Beneath the city’s pale towers and violet enchantments, a shared inheritance remained contested. Each hoped the sword would return to hands worthy of the history their people remembered.

A disguise opened the way to guarded knowledge. Suspicion and old allegiances stood around the history of the dragonforged blades, and the seeker recovered it under a borrowed appearance. The pages offered something steel alone could not restore. Before the broken hilt could become a weapon again, its name and the burden of its past had to be understood.

chapters.title: A blade remembered
chapters.body:
The recovered history gave the hilt a name: Quel’Delar, sister to Quel’Serrar. Its past bound the red dragonflight’s craft to the high elven crown and a defender who stood before the Sunwell. A gift had endured beyond a kingdom’s wound. Yet remembering the blade did not settle who might bear it next, or how its broken length could be restored.

In the older memory, Alexstrasza gave the blade to Anasterian, who later entrusted it to Thalorien Dawnseeker. The gift passed from a dragon to a king and onward to a defender. Quel’Thalas’s fate would test the inheritance. Beside the Sunwell’s ancient light, the sword’s promise waited upon the courage of the hand that carried it.

During the Third War, the Scourge reached Quel’Thalas. Thalorien held the approach before the Sunwell and fell buying time for those behind him. His defense could not spare the kingdom its wound, but his name remained bound to the blade he bore. Long afterward, another search would seek to restore what had survived that loss.

At Quel’Delar’s Rest, Lana’thel brought a darker memory. After Thalorien’s fall, the sword had passed into her hands. As the Lich King’s servant, she was ordered to destroy it. She carried Quel’Delar north and broke it there. A knight’s last defense and a queen’s enslavement now met in the shattered steel lying beneath the snow.

The breaking had not ended Quel’Delar’s history. Myralion vowed that the Sunreavers would restore it, while Caladis led the Silver Covenant’s separate search. Their resolve gave purpose to the work ahead. The blade had to be remade, the will within it faced, and the touch left by the Scourge cleansed. Beyond the hilt’s recovery waited a more perilous restoration.

chapters.title: Make the blade whole
chapters.body:
In the Pit of Saron, infused bars and a forgehammer joined the blade’s broken length. The mine lay beneath Icecrown, a place of forced labor and dark ore within the frozen land. Quel’Delar became whole again. Yet the material that held its pieces carried a peril of its own, and the restored weapon had not been freed from the darkness around its making.

The joined blade was carried to the Crucible of Souls within the Forge of Souls. There it was tempered amid the machinery of the Lich King’s frozen halls. The weapon had regained its shape, but its next passage would expose a deeper difficulty. An edge made whole could still bear a spirit that had not been cleansed.

Quel’Delar pressed its bearer toward the Halls of Reflection. The blade possessed a will, and its command led into the Lich King’s chamber. Within the blue-black hall, the search for restoration became a struggle for mastery. A finished edge could be carried in the hand; the power directing that hand now had to be confronted.

The seeker resisted Quel’Delar’s command and brought its will to heel. The sword survived the struggle, yet restraint did not make it pure. Icecrown’s dark ore still held the repaired steel together. A voice within the chamber would name what the reforging had carried into it, and the search would turn from mastery toward cleansing.

Uther’s spirit named the deeper wound: saronite was the blood of an Old God, and its taint had entered the restored blade. His counsel turned the seeker toward the Sunwell. Beyond Icecrown’s frozen halls lay older light, in a sacred place the blood elves had reclaimed. There the sword might be cleansed of what its new forging had forced into it.

chapters.title: Light and inheritance
chapters.body:
At Quel’Danas, Halduron Brightwing refused entry to the sacred place the blood elves had recently reclaimed. The Sunwell’s shores carried the memory of a kingdom nearly lost. Before the dangerous blade could reach its light, the seeker had to earn trust. Beyond the Dead Scar, the journey approached those whose duty was to guard that inheritance.

At Thalorien’s resting place, the seeker faced a trial and the memory of the fallen knight. His death remained in the Third War, yet his blessing could reach the bearer who now carried his blade. The past had not returned him to life. It offered a bond between the defender’s sacrifice and the burden of restoring what had survived him.

At last, the tempered blade was lowered into the Sunwell. Its light cleansed the saronite taint, and Quel’Delar emerged purified. Thalorien’s sacrifice and Lana’thel’s enslavement remained part of its history. What changed was the inheritance the living could carry. Broken and remade, the sword left the sacred waters free of the darkness that had entered its steel.

The restored blade returned toward Dalaran along the paths of the Silver Covenant and Sunreavers. Each people could welcome the recovery without ending the rivalry around its inheritance. Among the blood elves, Aethas could present a new bearer. Yet no single name settled the sword’s future for all. Quel’Delar’s long passage through gift, sacrifice and corruption had reached the hope of restoration.

storylines.reviewNote: Research story with secondary quest transcripts and a secondary mirror of an archived Blizzard article. Original Wrath 3.3.5a quest text, relative flashback dates, and faction variants need client comparison and editor review. Randomized loot is a gameplay trigger; Alliance and Horde lines are alternatives; Thalorien’s historical death is distinct from his later quest test; no named adventurer is canonical. Generated art is interpretive; in-client area/model resemblance review remains open.

storylines.title: Ras Frostwhisper: a lich’s mortality
storylines.summary: A magistrate seeks a relic of Ras Frostwhisper’s mortal life. Stromgarde, Light’s Hope, Stratholme and Scholomance lead to Leonid’s account and an attempt to bind the lich to his former self.
storylines.opening: A ruined city yields a small remnant; an old witness gives it a history. Bound to the soul of a fallen mage, the keepsake carries a mortal memory toward the lich in Scholomance.

chapters.title: A remnant of mortal life
chapters.body:
At Caer Darrow, Magistrate Marduke appeared to those who could see the dead. He sought a way into Ras Frostwhisper’s mortal past. A keepsake from Stromgarde, the ruined city he called Ras’s home, might give that lost life a hold upon the present. Before the lich could be confronted, something of the man he had been had to be found.

Among Stromgarde’s broken stones, the seeker searched for a possession from Ras’s human life. The fallen city held the beginning of another man’s history beneath its own ruin. A small surviving object might reach where force alone could not. Beyond the abandoned walls waited the lich, whose old home could still yield a memory he had left behind.

A keepsake survived among the ruins. Marduke believed it could help create an artifact capable of reaching Ras. Its value lay in the life it recalled rather than the strength of its making. Carried toward Light’s Hope Chapel, the small possession joined a fallen city to the hope that a bond with the mortal past might endure beneath undeath.

At Light’s Hope Chapel, Leonid Barthalomew received the keepsake. Marduke had heard that Ras surrendered himself in Stratholme; Leonid might know more. The search had reached a witness among those who understood the dead. Before the token could serve its purpose, the seeker needed to learn how the man of Stromgarde had become the lich they meant to face.

chapters.title: A witness and a tainted ground
chapters.body:
Leonid remembered Ras pledging his soul to the Lich King and ending his own mortal life. His body fell upon marked ground. In Leonid’s recollection, the Lich King stood over the fallen mage, and Ras rose as a lich. The witness’s memory gave the old rumor a terrible shape, binding the keepsake’s human past to a chosen surrender.

Leonid named the place Menethil’s Gift: ground blessed by the Lich King and held holy by the Scourge. The name carried a bitter inheritance. He sent the seeker back to Stratholme with the keepsake, toward the place where Ras had yielded his mortal life. There the small possession might gain a bond with the soul its memory recalled.

At Menethil’s Gift, the keepsake was placed upon the tainted ground. A soul could cling to what recalled its former life, and the object became bound to that fallen soul. Its change offered the means the search had sought. Yet the bond had not been tested against Ras, and the hope carried from Stromgarde still awaited its encounter with the lich.

The Soulbound Keepsake returned to Light’s Hope. Leonid believed its connection to the fallen soul should also hold to Ras’s physical form. The object had changed; whether it could reach the lich remained to be learned. He sent it onward to Marduke, carrying an explanation and a possibility toward the magistrate whose inquiry had begun among memories of a mortal home.

At Caer Darrow, Marduke received the transformed keepsake and prepared the seeker for its use. The search could now turn toward Scholomance. From ruined streets, a witness’s memory and tainted ground, the living had gathered a means to confront Ras through his own past. The old academy sheltered the lich whose human life the object still recalled.

chapters.title: The lich and the keepsake
chapters.body:
Within Scholomance’s cold halls, the seeker found Ras Frostwhisper. The keepsake was brought within reach of the mage who had chosen undeath. All that had been gathered now met the form it was meant to change. A possession from Stromgarde’s ruins stood against the power that had carried its former owner beyond his mortal life.

The keepsake reached Ras through the bond with his former life. His undead form gave way to a mortal one. The change opened a brief and terrible possibility; it did not offer a restored life beyond the encounter. The man recalled by the token could be struck down, and Marduke’s purpose now approached its final cost.

Ras was killed in mortal form, and his head was carried back to Marduke. The keepsake had undone his undead guise long enough for that blow to fall. What became of his spirit remained unknown. From the ruined home to Scholomance’s cold halls, the search had recovered a bond with the past and used it for a reckoning rather than a return to life.

At Caer Darrow, Marduke received the head and declared that ten thousand restless souls had cried out at the blow against the Scourge. His words gave the deed its meaning, while Ras’s own soul remained beyond the seeker’s knowledge. The lich had been made mortal and killed. The inquiry ended with the magistrate’s declaration, leaving the dead their unanswered silence.

storylines.reviewNote: Complete illustrated research story with 13 original transcript scenes, a claim/citation record per beat, Classic-region environments, distinct representations for Marduke, Leonid, Ras’s lich and recalled human states, and the keepsake and final quest object. It belongs to the Classic-to-Wrath StoryTour and remains outside the EraTour. Quest text comes from secondary Classic mirrors; original-client/build comparison, the Stratholme sigil-room locator, lore/citation approval, all environment/figure resemblance comparisons, and voice audition remain open. Ras’s post-quest spirit and the fate of the “ten thousand” souls are not supplied.

storylines.title: The Scepter of the Shifting Sands
storylines.summary: A shattered key joins an ancient war’s grief to the later recovery of its fragments, the labor of rival peoples and the opening of the Scarab Wall.
storylines.opening: A wall built to contain the qiraji outlived the war that raised it. A thousand years later, the danger behind that barrier brought rival peoples to Silithus, where the broken scepter had to be made whole before the gates could open.
storylines.reviewNote: Complete 22-scene research telling with an illustrated, non-geographic theater and optional AI narration. Quest facts are checked against accessible reproductions of original game text and Blizzard accounts; original-client/build comparison and human claim review remain required before publication. The ancient prologue is Era 5; the later quest journey is Era 8. Parallel shard branches are presented in an editorial order, not a mandatory canonical chronology. Realm quotas, timers and Scarab Lord identities are not universal history. No post-Wrath outcomes are included.

chapters.title: Flashback · Era 5 — The war that raised the wall
chapters.body: Long before the adventurers came to Silithus, the night elves had fought a war beneath its harsh southern sky. Fandral Staghelm led their defense against the qiraji, and his son Valstann fell in the struggle. The dragonflights joined the battle, but neither courage nor ancient power could make the loss undone. As the defenders were driven toward Ahn'Qiraj, the question before them became how to contain an enemy they could not wholly destroy. The wall that later generations would find was born of that necessity.

chapters.title: Flashback · Era 5 — A victory without comfort
chapters.body: At the gate, Merithra, Arygos and Caelestrasz held the enemy back while Anachronos and the defenders raised the barrier. When the seal was made, the bronze dragon offered Fandral a scepter and a gong: a means to open the way if the need returned. Fandral would accept no further burden from that victory. His son was gone; the stronghold still stood. He cast the scepter against the barrier and shattered it. Anachronos gathered the fragments, preserving a duty that grief had refused.

chapters.title: The keepers of a broken promise
chapters.body: The broken scepter did not pass out of history. Its pieces remained in the keeping of dragons, yet the long vigil brought troubles of its own. When Anachronos later named Eranikus, Vaelastrasz and Azuregos, his warning carried the weight of disappointed trust. Each guardian's story had turned toward tragedy or estrangement. To restore the key, mortal seekers would have to enter those stories. A thousand years separated the wars, but time had not protected the watchers from the wounds of the world.

chapters.title: The road from Cenarion Hold
chapters.body: The later journey began in Silithus, where Baristolth of the Shifting Sands directed seekers toward the bronze dragon at the Caverns of Time. Anachronos did not simply place the world's burden in the first hands that reached him. The path demanded evidence of resolve. It led into Blackwing Lair, to Broodlord Lashlayer, before the deeper work of gaining the brood's trust. The task was already larger than one traveler: a champion's progress depended upon companions willing to enter the mountain together.

chapters.title: The memory at the Scarab Wall
chapters.body: Before seeking the scattered pieces, the adventurers returned to the place where the bond had broken. At the Scarab Wall, the old struggle was shown again: dragons pressing back the qiraji, defenders reaching the barrier, and Fandral turning away from the offered key. This was no new battle in Silithus. It was the past made visible to those who would inherit its unfinished task. The scepter could open a gate; the memory explained why that gate had first been closed, and why its key had been rejected.

chapters.title: Red shard — The captive guardian
chapters.body: In Blackwing Lair, Vaelastrasz could no longer fulfill his charge by surrendering the red shard. Nefarian held it, and threatened to destroy it. The wounded red dragon's appeal made the recovery urgent: the loss of that fragment would deny the seekers their key to Ahn'Qiraj. Here the search for an ancient relic entered a living act of cruelty. The adventurers had to carry Vaelastrasz's last request through the fortress of the very enemy who had brought him low.

chapters.title: Red shard — Beyond the dragon’s suffering
chapters.body: Nefarian fell, and the red fragment was recovered before he could destroy it. When the shard returned, Anachronos spoke of Vaelastrasz’s soul finding rest. The recovery fulfilled a guardian’s charge after his own strength had failed him. One piece of the scepter was safe again, but the cost of its keeping would remain within the history of the restored artifact.

chapters.title: Green shard — A guardian lost to the Nightmare
chapters.body: The green trail began beneath the marshes, in the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Near the Shade of Eranikus, Malfurion's appearance directed the search beyond the temple and toward his agent in Teldrassil. From the forest wisp, the road led to Keeper Remulos in Moonglade. The green shard could not be reclaimed by treating its guardian as another enemy to be slain. The search had reached a dragon ensnared by the Nightmare, and the help it sought would have to reach him through that corruption.

chapters.title: Green shard — The gathering of corruption
chapters.body: Remulos's preparations sent the adventurers to the forest portals associated with the Dream. The search ranged through Duskwood, Ashenvale, Feralas and the Hinterlands, gathering the fragments needed for the next confrontation. These were separate places bound by one danger, rather than a single road across the forest. The journey widened the threat beyond the temple where it had begun. By returning with the corruption's traces, the seekers made possible the attempt to draw Eranikus into Moonglade, where his redemption could be sought.

chapters.title: Green shard — Restraint at Nighthaven
chapters.body: When Eranikus entered Nighthaven, the duty was to endure him, not to kill him. Keeper Remulos had to survive, and the settlement had to be defended while Tyrande approached. The dragon's assault and the shades of the Nightmare made that restraint costly. Yet destroying him would defeat the purpose for which the defenders had gathered. Their task was to hold the space in which rescue remained possible: to stand against his violence without surrendering the hope that the guardian beneath it could be freed.

chapters.title: Green shard — The guardian returns
chapters.body: Tyrande's arrival brought the intervention the defenders had awaited. Eranikus was redeemed, and Remulos spoke of his return to the Dream to confront the wrong he had done. The green fragment could now be carried back to Anachronos. Unlike the red trail, this recovery left its guardian able to return to his own work. The two journeys shared a broken scepter, but their endings were different: one honored a lost watcher; the other restored a watcher to the struggle from which he had fallen.

chapters.title: Blue shard — A dragon who wished to be left alone
chapters.body: On Azshara's coast, Azuregos offered a very different account of guardianship. The shard had drawn attention he did not want, interrupting his study of the ancient shore. He had hidden it with an enchanted fish, making an ordinary search of the sea hopeless. His solution for its recovery was an arcanite buoy that would draw the creature out. The instructions lay in a ledger, and the ledger had to be taken to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris. The blue trail began with a dragon's evasion and became an engineer's problem.

chapters.title: Blue shard — From Silverpine to Molten Core
chapters.body: Narain needed his missing scrying goggles before his work could continue. The search led to Stewvul, his former friend, hiding in a crate near the Greymane Wall. He no longer had them, and the seekers went on to Molten Core. A quarrel between gnomes had carried the great undertaking beneath Blackrock Mountain, binding a small loss to the fate of unopened gates.

chapters.title: Blue shard — The chef and the Isle of Dread
chapters.body: Another of Narain's demands led to Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan. The chef's answer sent the adventurers out to the Isle of Dread, off Feralas, to hunt the chimaerok and secure the ingredients for his formidable meal. The scale of the task belonged to the same curious bargain as the goggles: the world's key depended upon satisfying the engineer's requirements. This branch brought the search from desert workshops to a dangerous island, where even preparing a feast called for allies rather than a solitary traveler.

chapters.title: Blue shard — A ransom in the snow
chapters.body: The search for Narain's book brought back a ransom letter instead of the missing volume. Its captors demanded payment, and Narain answered with a deception of his own. He gave the adventurers clothing to take his place and a sack of rocks to stand for gold. The appointed meeting lay in Winterspring, far from his desert home. There the false payment brought the seekers into the encounter with Number Two. The scheme did not recover the book; its pages still had to be gathered by another road.

chapters.title: Blue shard — A book scattered to the winds
chapters.body: Doctor Weavil had intervened in the search for Draconic for Dummies, and Narain’s book lay torn into eight chapters. Narain supplied a magical binding, but the pages had to be recovered. Before the scepter could become whole, another broken object demanded restoration. Across distant lands, the words needed to understand Azuregos’s ledger waited upon the companions who sought the blue shard.

chapters.title: Blue shard — Libraries, demons, and dragon lairs
chapters.body: The missing chapters drew the adventurers through places that rarely belonged to one journey. Pages awaited in Stormwind and Undercity, in the dangerous reaches of Winterspring and the Blasted Lands, and on Doctor Weavil's Alcaz Island. Others required the company to return to Blackwing Lair, confront Onyxia, and reach Ragnaros in Molten Core. A single scattered volume bound these distant dangers to the same unfinished work. The reconstructed volume gave Narain the means to continue the work Azuregos had set before him.

chapters.title: Blue shard — The beast in the Bay of Storms
chapters.body: With the preparations complete, the blue trail returned to the sea. Narain sent the adventurers to the Bay of Storms in Azshara with the arcanite buoy, warning them of Maws. The creature that held the shard could be drawn from hiding, but recovering it demanded companions ready for the danger that answered. When the blue fragment was won, the instructions were at last simple: carry it to Anachronos. An old dragon's elaborate concealment had become a journey through much of Azeroth before ending on its storm-bound coast.

chapters.title: The key and the armies
chapters.body: The three fragments returned to Anachronos, and the scepter could be made whole. Beyond the seekers’ long journey, Horde and Alliance communities gathered supplies for a campaign in Silithus. Workshops, stores and countless contributions prepared the force that would face the opened stronghold. Rival peoples approached one threshold, carrying both their divisions and a shared duty. The coming battle needed the restored artifact and the labor of many hands.

chapters.title: The gates open
chapters.body: When the preparations had brought the campaign to the Scarab Wall, the restored scepter could be raised against the gong. The barrier made by the ancient defenders opened, and the danger it had contained came forth. The ensuing struggle was remembered as the Ten-Hour War. The relic's recovery had not ended the conflict; it had made the confrontation possible. Where Fandral once turned away from the gate in grief, a later generation now stood together before the consequences of opening it.

chapters.title: Beyond the wall, beneath the temple
chapters.body: The campaign continued into the Ruins and the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj. Beyond the qiraji armies lay C'Thun, the deeper threat against which the preparations had been gathered. Victory there gave the opened gate its purpose: the company had not restored a key merely to release what waited behind the wall. It had restored a way to reach that danger. The victory brought this campaign to its close, after a long road from the bronze dragon’s vigil. The scepter's legacy joins the losses of the first war to the collective labor of the second.

chapters.title: The journey that outlived the gong
chapters.body: After the opening war, the restored scepter brought its bearers another recognition from the Timeless One. The journey had reached beyond the moment at the gong. Across forests, libraries, mountains and seas, companions had gathered around a broken promise. Its completion honored the long recovery and the watchers whose charges had failed or endured, as well as the threshold their work had allowed the world to cross.

storylines.title: The Scythe of Elune: The Original Mystery
storylines.summary: An Ashenvale inquiry follows Velinde Starsong’s journal across ports to Duskwood. A separate witness account deepens the trail without resolving who next held the Scythe or making every worgen mystery one cause.
storylines.opening: At a ruined Ashenvale shrine, a tome preserves a missing priestess’s memory. Her journal carries the search across ports toward Duskwood, where another witness recalls a weapon found and lost. Their separate accounts meet at Roland’s Doom, leaving the Scythe’s next keeper unknown.

chapters.title: The shrine and the journal
chapters.body:
At Forest Song, Melyria spoke of demons pressing out of Felwood and a ruined shrine overtaken by mysterious wolf-men. Their cries had given the hollow its name. She asked the seeker to read the Tome of Mel’Thandris. Amid the forest’s unrest, a sacred ruin and a strange pack held the beginning of a mystery no sentinel could yet explain.

The Tome revealed a memory of Velinde Starsong. As her companions dwindled and her strength failed against the demons, she called to Elune. In the vision, she received the Scythe and believed her prayer answered. Melyria saw more to investigate. A gift had entered the struggle, but the memory had not yet shown what its power would bring into the forest.

Melyria sent the inquiry to Thyn’tel Bladeweaver in Darnassus. Velinde had served at Forest Song before her disappearance. Thyn’tel hesitated to open her belongings to a stranger; the Sentinels still hoped their trusted priestess might return. Between the shrine’s vision and the effects preserved in the city, the search approached a life left unfinished in the memory of her people.

The vision persuaded Thyn’tel to lend the key to Velinde’s chest. Within it lay a journal. Its pages preserved the priestess’s work and doubts, carrying her own understanding of the Scythe. The city had kept those belongings in hope of her return. Now her writing offered a way to follow what she had believed and what had troubled her before she vanished.

Velinde wrote that the Scythe let her speak with the worgen and summon them into her world. The first pack followed her against the demons in Felwood. To the embattled priestess, they offered allies where her own companions had become too few. The wolf-men at Mel’Thandris now stood within a darker question: what else had entered the forest with that desperate hope?

The journal’s later pages darkened. Packs grew when Velinde no longer summoned them, and one sent into the forest never returned. She feared their leaders had passed beyond her control. Leaving the worgen she could gather at the shrine, she sought knowledge in Darnassus and Darkshore. A rumor that Arugal had summoned worgen offered another lead, and she decided to seek the wizard.

chapters.title: A trail of records
chapters.body:
Velinde’s last entry planned a passage from a Barrens port toward the lead concerning Arugal. Thyn’tel sent the seeker to Wharfmaster Dizzywig in Ratchet. The priestess had left an intention rather than an answer. Beyond her final written words, people along the docks might remember where the search had carried her, and whether the hope in those pages had survived the crossing.

At Ratchet, Dizzywig found Velinde’s name beside passage on the Black Osprey to Booty Bay. With no contrary entry, he believed the ship had arrived safely. The ledger offered a named crossing and a likely destination, though no message from Velinde herself. Across the sea, a caravaner might remember what followed her arrival upon the farther shore.

In Booty Bay, Ruzzgot remembered a night elf priestess travelling with his caravan. They parted upon the northbound road, and he recalled her heading toward Darkshire. The search entered Duskwood, where worgen were already feared. From a ship’s ledger to a traveller’s memory, the trail carried Velinde’s absence toward the town whose records might preserve another sign of her passage.

Clerk Daltry found no record of Velinde staying at the inn. Yet he knew of the wolf-men the seeker described and pointed toward the Carevin household. Their hunters opposed the wood’s monsters. Darkshire had yielded no remembered lodging for the missing priestess, but the creatures linked to her search offered another way onward, toward a mine south of the town.

Jonathan Carevin knew the place where worgen had first been found in Duskwood. He asked that Roland’s Doom be searched for a sign of the Scythe. The priestess’s passage remained unconfirmed, and the weapon’s fate unknown. Beneath the forest’s older fears, the mine might hold a trace of the loss that had drawn the search so far from Ashenvale.

chapters.title: Two accounts at Roland’s Doom
chapters.body:
At a mound within Roland’s Doom, Velinde’s specter appeared. She spoke of failure, worgen beyond control and the loss of Elune’s Scythe. Whose hand now directed it, she did not know. The seeker had reached the priestess’s grief, but not the weapon. Beyond her testimony, the moment of her death and the Scythe’s next bearer remained hidden.

Carevin heard what the mine had revealed. He promised to make the worgen’s numbers a priority, though the root of the danger remained beyond his household’s reach. The weapon was still lost. Resistance could be offered where a cure could not. The seeker returned toward Darnassus, carrying Velinde’s grief to those who had kept her belongings in hope.

Thyn’tel received the report as news of Velinde’s fate. A trusted friend had been lost, and the Scythe had passed beyond her people’s keeping. The search ended without recovering it or naming its new bearer. Darnassus could remember the priestess and acknowledge her loss. It could not yet tell where the power she had once welcomed had gone.

Separate testimony survived in a partial book from Sven’s farm, later linked to Jitters. Its writer remembered finding a scythe in Roland’s Doom. Worgen attacked after he pulled it free, and he fled, losing it along the way. He wondered whether his act had brought them, but could not know. Another witness narrowed the mystery to Duskwood without revealing the weapon’s next keeper.

storylines.reviewNote: Complete illustrated research story with 15 transcript nodes, nine Classic Scythe quest beats, an independent Sven/Jitters Duskwood witness record, a claim and citation ledger, dedicated Classic-area scenes and cast/object art, and matching narration tracks. All records remain contentStatus research. The two chains are joined editorially, not as quest prerequisites. The story keeps attribution and uncertainty, gives no exact date, route or unproved Duskwood causality, and excludes Gilneas/Cataclysm, later comics, post-Cataclysm area states and the Legion artifact campaign. Original-client quest/item capture, Classic-area/cast comparison, citation/claim review and narration audition remain open. The included Classic accounts do not identify the Scythe’s subsequent bearer; Jitters’s recovered object is not proven to be the same item.

storylines.title: The Shattered Sun and the restored Sunwell
storylines.summary: Kael’thas turns toward the Sunwell to summon Kil’jaeden. Blood elves and draenei join the Shattered Sun Offensive across Quel’Danas and parallel Outland fronts; the Sunwell Plateau campaign ends in Anveena’s sacrifice and Velen’s renewal of the fount.
storylines.opening: The old fount remembers a lost home. Now Kael’thas has returned to Silvermoon, the Sunwell is threatened again, and blood elves and draenei gather together beneath Shattrath’s light.

chapters.title: A fount raised for a new home
chapters.body: Long before this campaign, exiles from Kalimdor crossed to the northern Eastern Kingdoms and made Quel’Thalas their home. There, at a convergence of arcane power, they raised the Sunwell. Its waters became a center of their new nation and a source the blood elves would later struggle to live without. The people built their home around the fount, and all that followed would be measured against its loss.

chapters.title: The fount falls
chapters.body: When the Scourge reached Quel’Thalas, its advance ended in ruin for the kingdom. Arthas Menethil corrupted the Sunwell in the course of that invasion. The fount that had sustained the high elves was lost, leaving the surviving blood elves to seek other ways through their hunger for magic. Its loss cast a long shadow across the years ahead.

chapters.title: The returning prince
chapters.body: After his defeat in Outland, Kael’thas returned to Silvermoon. He betrayed the people he had promised to lead and turned toward a new design: using the Sunwell to summon Kil’jaeden. Thus the fount became an immediate danger once more, and an inheritance the blood elves could not reclaim. In Shattrath, blood elves and draenei joined the Shattered Sun Offensive against Kael’thas and the Legion. The coalition crossed old divisions to confront a threat aimed at Quel’Thalas. Heroes of the Horde and Alliance also took part; together, they turned toward the endangered fount. From Shattrath came two calls to the isle’s work. Aldor agents sent the seeker north with “Crisis at the Sunwell,” while the Scryers offered “Duty Calls.” The choice began on opposite sides of the Terrace of Light, yet both led across the sea toward Quel’Danas and the staging ground near the fount.

chapters.title: The offensive on two fronts
chapters.body: The first position on the island is small and exposed. The Offensive arrives with limited forces near the Sunwell Plateau, where blood elves aligned with Kael’thas and demons hold the way inward. From that shorehead, the scattered coalition begins to press the island and its guarded approach. Across the sanctum, armory and harbor, the coalition presses against Kael’thas’s banners. Farther off, a portal opens toward Shattrath, widening the reach of the island front. Each gain brings the defenders nearer to the plateau and the fount they guard. The Offensive’s work reached back into Outland as well. Bands struck Sunfury holdings and gathered what the campaign needed, while other soldiers held the island front. Each force bore its own burden beneath the broken sky, far from the shore of Quel’Danas. An intelligence contact inside Magisters’ Terrace stops reporting. The Shattered Sun sends a search party into the blood-elf complex to find the missing spy and recover what they learned. Within those polished halls, the campaign meets another face of Kael’thas’s rule. Elsewhere on the isle, the Shattered Sun confronts Kael’thas within Magisters’ Terrace. His stand ends there; at the plateau, the Sunwell remains beneath his design. The prince is stopped, yet the fount itself is still in danger.

chapters.title: The campaign through Sunwell Plateau
chapters.body: Beyond the island’s outer battles lies Sunwell Plateau, where Kael’thas has turned the fount toward his summoning. Demons and corrupted light gather around the heart of Quel’Thalas. The defenders must cross the high sanctum and reach the well itself. At the edge of the inner sanctum, Sathrovarr holds Kalecgos in thrall. The blue dragon fights from within a shadowed realm even as allies face the dreadlord outside. When his captor’s hold breaks, Kalecgos is free to lend his strength to the defense. Above the Dead Scar, Madrigosa challenges Brutallus. The pit lord strikes the blue dragon down, and her fall dims the defenders’ hopes. Yet the fel blood spilled from Brutallus will not leave her body in peace. From Brutallus’s wound, fel blood spreads beneath Madrigosa and stirs the fallen dragon once more. She rises as Felmyst, her blue form emptied of its old grace and wreathed in green fire. The cost of the battle follows the attackers deeper into the plateau. Lady Sacrolash and Grand Warlock Alythess stand together before the deeper halls. Their crimson and violet powers guard the way toward M’uru. Together, the Eredar Twins form one last wall between the Offensive and the fount. Within the Shrine of the Eclipse, the Offensive reaches M’uru, the naaru taken from Silvermoon. Its light has darkened into Entropius, and the defenders are forced to destroy the captive they had hoped to save. A spark endures within the heart that remains. At the last chamber, Kil’jaeden rises from the Sunwell, and the portal he sought begins to take shape. Kalecgos and the blue dragonflight join the defense around the threatened fount. Only Anveena’s act can break the demon’s advance. As Kil’jaeden threatens to break through, Anveena turns her power against him. Her sacrifice weakens the demon, and the attackers drive him from the well. The light she gives is spent; still, taint remains in the waters below. The heroes banish Kil’jaeden from the fount and stop the summoning before the Legion can pour through. The immediate invasion is ended. Yet the Sunwell’s waters remain polluted, and the blood elves face a second peril: the loss of the fount around which their kingdom gathered. Kil’jaeden is gone, yet corruption still clouds the Sunwell. Regent Lord Lor’themar considers destroying it lest the sickness spread beyond the fount. A victory has spared Quel’Thalas from one catastrophe, but the price may yet be the heart of the kingdom. Then Velen comes to honor M’uru. Velen arrives with Lady Liadrin and recovers the spark that remains in M’uru’s heart. He turns it upon the tainted water, and the Sunwell shines again, bearing both arcane light and the naaru’s gift. Liadrin grieves for what the Blood Knights did to M’uru; Velen answers with hope for what may grow from the loss. The old danger is ended, while the future of the nation is left open.

storylines.reviewNote: Complete 21-scene illustrated research StoryGuide with transcript, per-scene source/citation/claim records, named raid figures and objects, separate TBC-era environmental states, and generated narration after voice production. The foundation and Scourge fall are labeled prologues; the Magisters’ Terrace, staged island phases and Outland tasks are not made one personal prerequisite chain. Server-wide objectives and patch release schedules are gameplay, not in-world dates. Secondary quest and raid locators remain unverified against the original patch-2.4 client; the Blizzard Timeline Chapter 14 header has a patch-2.3 discrepancy. Human lore/source review, TBC area/model resemblance review and audio audition remain open. No record is reviewed or published.

storylines.title: The Dragon in Stormwind
storylines.summary: A conspiracy reaches from the Burning Steppes into Stormwind’s court while a separate Horde intelligence path follows Rexxar toward Onyxia’s lair.
storylines.opening: The city seemed to rest behind pale stone and blue banners. Yet the black dragon’s influence had entered its court, and far away the Horde began a different search beneath the same mountain.

chapters.title: The Queen Behind the Court
chapters.body:
In the Burning Steppes, black dragonkin gather beneath a sky troubled by ash. Their attacks turn a frontier alarm into a question about the reach of the black dragonflight. The Alliance investigation begins with scattered signs and grows toward the mountain that shelters them. The evidence points to a danger with a foothold beyond the wilds; it does not yet reveal the hand guiding Stormwind’s court.

Reports from Redridge and the Burning Steppes carry the search into Stormwind. In the Keep, Bolvar Fordragon bears the kingdom’s regency while Countess Katrana Prestor speaks with unusual influence. To the investigators, the mystery is no longer only a nest of dragonkin: a trusted figure sits within the very hall they are trying to protect. The resemblance between rumor and conspiracy remains a question still to be proved.

Deep in Blackrock Depths, Marshal Windsor has been held away from the court whose danger he understands. His account is not enough by itself to undo the power that silenced him. The adventurers find a soldier who has carried the truth through imprisonment, and a trail of evidence scattered through the fortress. The mountain’s iron rooms have become the place where a political mystery waits for its missing proof.

A crumpled note points toward the fragments Windsor needs. The search passes through the forge and deeper chambers of Blackrock Mountain, where small pieces of a document matter more than the strength of the gates. Recovered evidence gives Windsor grounds to leave his cell and face the city again. This is the work of a rescue and an investigation together: one carries the other back into the light.

The escape from Blackrock Depths is hard won. Windsor leads the way through hostile halls while his rescuers hold open each turn in the passage. Stormwind cannot hear its witness while he remains beneath the mountain. When the group emerges, the marshal can return to the city and place what he knows before the people who must judge it.

Windsor comes back to Stormwind with the evidence gathered in Blackrock. The capital that once seemed distant from the frontier danger now becomes the stage for its reckoning. Bolvar receives the marshal’s return, and the city’s uneasy court gathers around the claim. The journey has changed the question: instead of asking whether the marshal can escape, the Alliance must decide whether it can hear him.

Before the assembled court, Katrana Prestor’s disguise falls away. The woman who had stood near Stormwind’s seat of power is revealed as Onyxia, the black dragon whose agents troubled the frontier. Dragonkin answer her presence, and Bolvar stands against the assault as the adventurers fight to defend the Keep. The conspiracy is exposed, yet Onyxia escapes the city. Stormwind has found its hidden enemy, not ended the danger.

From the capital, the road winds into blue-white winter and brings the adventurers to Haleh. The Dragon’s Eye is the token that opens her counsel, turning Stormwind’s revelation into preparation. She names the test that lies ahead: the blood of a mighty black dragon, taken high within Blackrock Spire. Frost will soon give way to furnace heat.

In Upper Blackrock Spire, the adventurers face General Drakkisath and bring his blood to Haleh. From that trial comes the Drakefire Amulet, a ward that allows its bearer to withstand Onyxia’s lair. The Alliance has gone from suspicion to exposure and now to preparation. The key is won; the descent into the dragon’s den waits ahead.

chapters.title: A Separate Road Through the Horde
chapters.body:
Far from Stormwind’s court, the Horde receives a separate summons in the Badlands. Orders point toward the stronghold of Blackrock Spire and the power held there. This path does not begin as an answer to Windsor’s investigation; it grows from Horde intelligence, leaders and obligations of its own. The same mountain appears on another horizon, where a different people must decide what its threat means.

At Orgrimmar, Eitrigg’s counsel turns the reports into a charge for the Horde. The old veteran understands the danger gathering around Blackrock and sends the adventurers back toward the stronghold with a clearer purpose. The city’s red stone and timber frame a different kind of authority from Stormwind’s court: experience offered in service to the Horde. Its path leads next to a contest for Blackrock Spire.

The Horde’s orders bring the adventurers against Warchief Rend Blackhand in Blackrock Spire. His defeat and the proof carried away from it fulfill the charge entrusted to them. The mountain holds more than one danger, and the struggle with Rend belongs to the Horde’s own contest of power. It is a separate road from Windsor’s rescue, even as both paths approach the black dragon’s shadow.

At Orgrimmar, Thrall speaks of the danger and sends the search outward toward Rexxar. The Warchief’s words widen the matter into a concern for the Horde itself. The tale now leaves the city’s red stone and timber for the open country. Ahead lies a champion whose life at the edge of society has made him known across Kalimdor.

Across Desolace, the adventurers seek Rexxar, a wandering champion of the Horde. His place between the wilds and settled life makes him the guide to a difficult next task. Here the great campaign narrows to a search for one champion moving through an immense, sparse land. Rexxar sets the terms for learning how an adventurer might pass the protections around Onyxia’s lair.

Rexxar’s instruction leads to Myranda the Hag in the blighted Western Plaguelands. Her magic prepares a means of taking a dragon’s shape, a disguise needed for the work to come. It does not make the adventurers dragons or erase their purpose; it is a temporary tool for passing the watchers of the mountain. In the scarred land, the Horde’s road turns from finding an ally to testing a dangerous deception.

In the heat and dark water of Dustwallow Marsh, Emberstrife tests the forged appearance and sends the adventurers to claim dragon skulls from distant guardians. Three trials await beneath different skies, where the black dragonflight and its rivals still shape the wilds. Emberstrife will accept each skull as part of his demand; Myranda’s borrowed shape must hold until the passage is won.

Three guardians stand in lands far apart: Chronalis beneath the Tanaris sun, Scryer amid Winterspring snow, and Somnus beneath the Swamp of Sorrows’ green canopy. Each place holds its own weather and color, and each dragon bears one part of the trial Emberstrife set. With the three skulls gathered, the Horde can complete his charge and carry Myranda’s borrowed shape toward the black dragon’s mountain.

Axtroz waits amid the windswept Wetlands, where rain and low cloud soften the coast. This final dragon trial completes the tribute demanded by Emberstrife. Across Kalimdor’s distant shores and the Eastern Kingdoms, each challenge has brought the adventurers nearer to the mountain. Now their road turns back to Blackrock, where Drakkisath waits.

The Horde returns to Upper Blackrock Spire to confront General Drakkisath. The blood taken from this powerful black dragon completes the trial Rexxar laid before them. The Alliance has passed through its own hands to reach Haleh; the Horde has followed its leaders and its own road. Their stories share a threshold, but each company bears a separate history.

Back with Rexxar, the adventurers receive the Drakefire Amulet. The token bears the protection gathered from every trial and opens the way before them. The Horde has come to this gate by a road all its own: through intelligence, Eitrigg’s counsel, Thrall’s word, Rexxar’s charge and a dragon’s blood. At the mountain’s foot, that labor gives way to a final descent.

chapters.title: Past the Mountain
chapters.body: The Drakefire Amulet opened the way to Onyxia’s Lair. Those who came from Stormwind and those who answered the Horde’s call had followed separate roads, each bearing a history of its own. Within the den, champions faced the black dragon. Fire shivered across the stone as she took wing, and the long preparations met the danger they had been made to withstand.

storylines.reviewNote: Complete illustrated research telling with 21 scenes, distinct Alliance and Horde chains, separate Drakefire Amulet attunement, and the original Classic lair encounter. The quest spine was mapped from accessible secondary Classic locators; original quest text/build comparison, in-client visual comparison and human lore/art review are still required before promotion. The chains are not an Alliance–Horde causal link or one canonical player. Later Wrath raid changes are excluded.

storylines.title: Swift Flight Form: the raven’s legacy
storylines.summary: A Druid follows Morthis Whisperwing from Moonglade’s sleeping barrows to Outland’s raven cult. The recovered book names Anzu; three separate shrine trials and the Southfury Moonstone prepare the confrontation, while Morthis’s final warning leaves the future open.
storylines.opening: The marsh refuge offers a promise: Morthis can teach the Stormcrow’s secrets, if a Druid is willing to follow the evidence. What begins as a troubling dream leads through an old book, three guarded essences, and a stone that can call the Raven God into reach.

chapters.title: A warning within the Dream
chapters.body:
Among Zangarmarsh’s spore towers and shallow waters, Morthis Whisperwing offered a druid the secrets of the swift stormcrow form. His teaching began with a trial. Beyond the refuge waited knowledge that could not be gained by strength alone. In the drowned green country, a promise of flight opened a search into an older danger, carried through sleepers, spirits and scattered memory.

Morthis prepared a ward from the materials the seeker brought him. A sleeper waited in Moonglade’s barrows, and waking him would require care. The search for knowledge had acquired a responsibility to the one who kept it. Before the druid could hear what the dormant witness knew, the ward had to offer protection against the danger of his awakening.

Beneath Moonglade’s pines, the Stormrage Barrow Dens kept their old silence. In the southern den, Clintar Dreamwalker stirred beneath Morthis’s ward. He woke confused, carrying the burden of what he had witnessed. His spirit had to be followed beyond the waking world, where the divided soul could speak more freely than the body left behind.

Within a dream echo, Clintar’s spirit led the seeker toward three Relics of Aviana. Dreamwarden Lurosa helped keep the passage open. An Aspect of the Raven threatened the work. Clintar feared an outside presence, but that remained the witness’s suspicion. The relics were recovered from the dream, while the cause of its danger remained a question to carry back.

Morthis received the relics and Clintar’s warning. Neither could fully explain what had entered the Dream. If an older raven tradition held a clue, its history might still be found in Outland. He sent the seeker toward Arthorn Windsong in the Evergrove. The search turned from tending a sleeping guardian toward a memory that had outlasted its keepers.

chapters.title: The raven’s broken history
chapters.body:
The Evergrove offered green shelter among Blade’s Edge’s broken ridges. There Arthorn Windsong studied an old raven cult. Her work promised a lead without yet explaining Clintar’s fear. The druids needed to recover a history scattered and buried. Before a dangerous power could be confronted, the quiet grove became a place of study, drawing the search toward those who remembered its lost book.

Arthorn’s notes and Timeon’s clue led to Sai’kkal near the Vortex Pinnacle. A Seer’s Stone and an aether ray’s eye let the seeker perceive the arakkoa shade. Sai’kkal spoke of a raven book stolen, broken apart and buried. Its pieces lay at Skettis. The scattered words might name what troubled Clintar, if the lost work could be made whole enough to read.

From Blade’s Edge, the search turned toward Nagrand’s open grasslands. On Twilight Ridge, Watcher Elaira knew a way to seek what lay hidden. Beyond the spirit’s testimony waited buried fragments that the druid could not readily find. A living creature’s keen sight might reach them, carrying the search from broken memory toward the ground where its scattered words remained.

A wild sparrowhawk was trained to find the buried Raven Stones at Skettis. When its help was no longer needed, it would be released. For a time, the bird’s sight became an ally to the druids’ search. What memory and testimony had left incomplete could now be recovered from the earth, and the old book might yield the name they sought.

At Skettis, the Raven Stones were gathered and Arthorn reconstructed the book. Its words named Anzu as the Raven God and described three bird spirits bound to shrines. A name had emerged from the fragments, though the recovered prophecy still demanded care. The druid now faced separate trials in Terokkar, seeking the power needed to bring the dangerous being within reach.

chapters.title: Three essences of Terokkar
chapters.body:
At the first shrine, the Eagle guardian confronted the seeker. Its defeat yielded an essence to carry onward. The Bone Wastes held old places whose meanings had not vanished with their keepers. One spirit’s power had been gathered, but the preparation was incomplete. Two more shrines awaited the druid whose search had begun among the refuge’s green waters.

Beside Lake Ere’Noru, another shrine held the Falcon guardian. The seeker prevailed, and its essence joined the Eagle’s. Each spirit guarded its own place, each encounter adding to the preparation Arthorn had named. Beyond the lake remained Sorrow Wing Point. The Raven God had been identified, but the means to confront him still depended upon the last shrine’s challenge.

At Sorrow Wing Point, the Hawk guardian held the final shrine. Its defeat brought the third essence into the seeker’s hands. Eagle, Falcon and Hawk had each marked a separate trial. Together their powers could return to Cenarion Refuge, where Morthis would judge the preparation. The old book had supplied a name; the druid still needed a way to summon its bearer.

The essences returned to Cenarion Refuge with Arthorn’s report. Morthis warned that Anzu was powerful, and the trials had not yet made a direct summons possible. Another object had to be recovered. Knowledge and readiness had brought the druid this far, but the Raven God remained beyond reach until the means of calling him could be placed within the seeker’s hands.

chapters.title: A summons and an open threat
chapters.body:
In Azshara, the search for the Southfury Moonstone became a pursuit involving Rizzle Sprysprocket. The stone was recovered. Its purpose gave the final preparation a focus: the druids hoped to use it to summon Anzu. Open country now gave way to the halls of Auchindoun, where the object could bring the Raven God into the confrontation the old book had made possible.

Beneath Sethekk Halls’ broken arches, the Moonstone was placed in the Raven’s Claw. Anzu answered. The druid confronted and defeated him, gaining the swift stormcrow form Morthis had promised. The search had crossed dream and waking lands to reach this reckoning. Yet a victory over the Raven God could not promise that every danger to the Dream had ended.

At Cenarion Refuge, Morthis warned that Anzu’s followers might help him rise again. The Moonstone was kept for another day. The stormcrow’s knowledge had been won, and the Raven God defeated, but vigilance remained. Beyond the recovered book and the broken halls lay an unanswered future, entrusted to those who would remember the warning and keep watch.

storylines.title: Tirion and Taelan: Of Love and Family
storylines.summary: Tirion asks a stranger to help his son remember his family and honor. A childhood gift, a lost emblem and Renfray’s portrait reach Taelan in Hearthglen; his choice to leave ends in death and gives Tirion a renewed purpose.
storylines.opening: At the edge of the Plaguelands, an exile entrusts his son’s past to a stranger. Keepsakes carry a father’s hope into Hearthglen, where a choice to return leads toward the loss Tirion must bear.

chapters.title: An Exile’s Request
chapters.body:
In the cold Eastern Plaguelands, an old hermit accepted help before offering his name. Among the countryside’s dangers, a stranger earned his trust. At the riverbank, another wound waited beyond the work of survival: a family’s long absence. The land had lost much to plague and war; the hermit carried a loss whose living answer remained close enough to hope for.

The hermit was Tirion Fordring, convicted of treason and banished from the Alliance. He had remained near his son. Taelan had become lord of Mardenholde and a Highlord of the Scarlet Crusade, an order Tirion believed fallen from the Silver Hand’s purpose. The exiled father asked for help. He hoped the honor they had once shared still endured beneath his son’s service.

In the Undercroft lay a miniature warhammer Tirion had once given Taelan. It was bound to a false grave and the childhood belief that his father was dead. Small enough for a young hand, the keepsake carried years of separation beneath a lie. Its recovery could not restore those years. It offered one remembered gift to place before the son who had grown beyond it.

After Uther’s death, Taelan had stood at Northdale and laid down the Silver Hand’s standard. Its emblem rested beneath the lake. Tirion asked that it be recovered. From dark water, the small sign of an abandoned allegiance returned to the living. Beside the childhood hammer, it could recall a part of Taelan’s own honor that the Scarlet Crusade had not created.

chapters.title: What the Portrait Keeps
chapters.body:
Tirion remembered happier family days and the portrait painted by his friend Renfray. At Caer Darrow, the artist’s ghost remained among the island’s ruins. Her work had preserved a likeness of people since divided by death and exile. The seeker came for that surviving canvas, hoping a memory once set in paint could still reach the son its subjects had lost.

Renfray’s direction led into Stratholme. In the Archivist’s room, the Fordring family portrait lay hidden behind a picture of twin moons. Amid the ruined city, a small work of family memory had survived. The search that began with a child’s gift and an abandoned emblem now recovered the faces of a life Taelan had once known.

The painting returned with Karandra and young Taelan beside Tirion. It restored their likeness without returning their lost years. For the exiled father, memory could at last be placed within his son’s reach. If Taelan would receive it, the portrait might recall a belonging older than the Scarlet banners under which he now served.

At Uther’s Tomb, Myranda received Tirion’s appeal and the gathered keepsakes. His former ally could help the seeker enter Hearthglen. Against pale memorial stone and plague-damaged grass, the father’s hope passed into another’s care. Beyond that last preparation, the old family tokens would be carried directly to Taelan, beneath the colors of the order Tirion feared had claimed him.

chapters.title: Dreams and Departure
chapters.body:
A disguise opened the way into Hearthglen. Under borrowed Scarlet colors, the seeker brought Tirion’s package to Taelan. The father remained in exile while the memories he had gathered crossed the guarded threshold. Within the stronghold, the portrait, hammer and emblem reached the Highlord. What they might awaken belonged to the son who received them.

Taelan recognized how long he had served as the Grand Crusader’s instrument. His father’s memory had endured beneath that service, and he chose to leave Hearthglen. The keepsakes offered a past from which he could make that choice. Red-and-white standards still surrounded him, but their claim upon his future had broken. The way toward Tirion now lay beyond the hall.

Taelan left the keep, and Scarlet Crusade forces opposed his departure. He had chosen to break with the order that shaped his adult life. Through Hearthglen, the struggle carried him toward the open road. Beyond the settlement stood a tower. The journey toward his father had become an ordeal, with the allegiance he had abandoned barring his way.

At the roadside tower, Grand Inquisitor Isillien killed Taelan. The son who had chosen to leave the Scarlet Crusade could no longer return to the father he hoped to meet. A small human post stood amid the wounded land, marking the end of that road. The long labor to restore memory had reached a cost no recovered keepsake could answer.

Tirion reached the tower too late. He defeated Isillien and grieved beside Taelan. The appeal begun at Thondroril had brought the father back into his son’s life only at its ending. Truth had been recovered, but the living voice that might have answered was gone. Beside the body, the old hope of reunion gave way to a grief that would demand another purpose.

At Taelan’s body, Tirion vowed to gather a new Order of the Silver Hand and return it to the defense of the world. The honor his son had once laid down could still guide the living. The vow did not undo the loss beside the tower. It carried the father’s grief beyond exile, toward a duty whose fulfillment still lay ahead.
