Beside the body, the old hope of reunion gave way to a grief that would demand another purpose.

storyNodes.title: A vow to rebuild the Silver Hand
storyNodes.narration: At Taelan’s body, Tirion vowed to gather a new Order of the Silver Hand and return it to the defense of the world. The honor his son had once laid down could still guide the living. The vow did not undo the loss beside the tower. It carried the father’s grief beyond exile, toward a duty whose fulfillment still lay ahead.

storyNodes.title: The empire stands beneath its last unbroken sky
storyNodes.narration: Ancient Kalimdor entered this age beneath the splendor of the kaldorei empire. Roads and cities answered to Queen Azshara, and the Well of Eternity shone beside her capital like a promise without limit. Few could see that the same concentration of power which made the court magnificent had also made the whole world vulnerable to one circle's choice.

storyNodes.title: A chosen circle turns the Well into a door
storyNodes.narration: Azshara's favored Highborne drew ever more deeply upon the Well. Their work ceased to be only the art of their own civilization: it became a doorway offered to a power beyond the world. The decision belonged to a privileged court, but every forest, city, and people of Kalimdor would be made to bear its consequence.

storyNodes.title: Beyond the gate waits a will vast as ruin
storyNodes.narration: The force answering the Highborne was the Burning Legion, and beyond its first hosts stood Sargeras. The portal was meant to become wide enough for that fallen titan to enter Azeroth. While demonic armies crossed ahead of him, the ritual continued. The danger beyond the gateway was greater still than the hosts already bringing ruin to the land.

storyNodes.title: The invasion enters through the heart of empire
storyNodes.narration: Demonic hosts came through Zin-Azshari, and the bright center of the empire became the source of its burning. The Legion's destruction spread beyond the capital, carrying devastation into the lands around it. The power gathered beside the Well had opened the way to an enemy whose purpose reached far beyond the queen's court, threatening the world that had sustained it.

storyNodes.title: A divided people chooses resistance
storyNodes.narration: Not all kaldorei followed the queen into catastrophe. Soldiers, priests, common defenders, and those who had questioned the court gathered against enemies both foreign and familiar. Their coalition was never one unchanging host. It grew while cities fell, drew strength from many kinds of loyalty, and learned that preserving the world might require opposing the order that had ruled it.

storyNodes.title: Three paths meet within one desperate war
storyNodes.narration: Malfurion listened for powers older than the court. Tyrande carried devotion into the struggle and held others together beneath fear. Illidan trusted dangerous knowledge and his own fierce judgment. Their purposes crossed, parted, and crossed again. None of them alone was the resistance, yet each choice would outlive the world in which it was made.

storyNodes.title: The living world answers the invaders
storyNodes.narration: The war could no longer be contained within kaldorei politics. Cenarius and other ancient powers joined the defense of the land itself, and the dragons entered the struggle from the sky. For a brief hour, beings divided by nature and history acted upon one truth: if the Legion prevailed, there would be no separate refuge left to guard.

storyNodes.title: The weapon of many answers to one will
storyNodes.narration: The Dragon Aspects gave their strength to an artifact meant to break the Legion's advance. Neltharion wielded it, then turned its power upon those who had trusted him. The betrayal wounded the alliance at the moment of greatest need. Victory could no longer depend upon one perfect weapon or upon the unity of the dragons.

storyNodes.title: The war returns to the water at its beginning
storyNodes.narration: Every surviving purpose narrowed again toward the Well. The defenders reached the gateway before Sargeras could cross, and the ritual was broken. Yet the portal had been joined too deeply to the power beneath it. Stopping the invasion did not restore the old world. It set loose a collapse no army, queen, dragon, or demigod could command.

storyNodes.title: One continent becomes a memory
storyNodes.narration: The Well collapsed. Seas rushed into the wound, the old land broke, and distances that had been crossed by road became oceans. At the center remained the Maelstrom, turning above the place where power and pride had drawn ruin together. Ancient Kalimdor was gone. The survivors would inherit separated shores where one vast continent had once stood.

storyNodes.title: The sea closes over the queen's old world
storyNodes.narration: Azshara and Highborne followers were taken beneath the waters, yet the depths did not end their history. They survived through transformation, while the cities that had proclaimed their permanence vanished below the new sea. Above them, the broken shores marked the end of their empire. Beneath the waves, the queen and her followers endured in altered forms.

storyNodes.title: Survivors carry the old world toward Hyjal
storyNodes.narration: The Sundering destroyed the old continent and forced survivors away from lands lost to the sea. Many defenders sought the surviving heights around Mount Hyjal, where they could regroup after the war. They came from different places and did not move as one company. At Hyjal, survival became a longer task: guarding a broken world and deciding which parts of the old one could be carried forward.

storyNodes.title: A winter road for the Alliance
storyNodes.narration: At the edge of Dragonblight, the Alliance advanced beneath blue and gold. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon led its host north against the Scourge, with the Wrathgate beyond the frozen ridges. The land offered little shelter from the Lich King’s shadow. The army moved toward Angrathar, where the Horde, too, had come to strike the same enemy. For a moment, separate campaigns gathered beneath one purpose.

storyNodes.title: The Kor’kron muster
storyNodes.narration: The Horde’s vanguard gathered beneath red banners in the same northern waste. Warlord Dranosh Saurfang held command at Angrathar, where the Scourge guarded the way to Icecrown. The Horde’s road was its own, yet the enemy beyond the gate was shared. The armies drew nearer from different positions, neither surrendering its colors as the field widened before the Lich King’s fortress.

storyNodes.title: Two banners beneath one gate
storyNodes.narration: At Angrathar, Bolvar and Dranosh led the two hosts into a common assault against the Scourge. The dark gate barred the road to Icecrown. Shields crossed beside shields beneath banners that had long met as rivals. Here, divided campaigns came face to face with the Lich King’s host. The attack gathered force before the gate, but it would not remain a battle only of steel.

storyNodes.title: The Lich King answers
storyNodes.narration: Arthas, crowned by the Frozen Throne, came out to meet the assault. Dranosh met him in the field; the Lich King struck him down with Frostmourne. Bolvar and the armies pressed onward against the undead, yet one of the Horde’s commanders was gone from the living. The gate’s horror was already at hand: the Scourge had not been the only danger waiting among the banners.

storyNodes.title: A betrayal in green fire
storyNodes.narration: Forsaken plague engines opened, and green fire and vapour rolled across the snow, taking the Scourge and the living armies alike. The Alliance and Horde had crossed the field against one enemy; now their ranks fell to the same substance. Bolvar vanished in the ruin. The source of the order lay beyond the stricken field, and no survivor there could yet answer who had set the attack in motion.

storyNodes.title: Fire from the red sky
storyNodes.narration: Then red wings came out of the northern sky. The Red Dragonflight poured cleansing fire across the blighted valley, breaking the plague’s hold on snow and stone. The battle ended, but the flame could not restore the fallen or return those lost behind its veil. What remained was a gate, a silent field, and two armies carrying different answers to the same catastrophe.

storyNodes.title: The report in Stormwind
storyNodes.narration: Word reached Stormwind that Bolvar and many of the Alliance had been lost at Angrathar. The first Alliance account treated the missing commander as dead and laid the gate’s betrayal at the Horde’s door. At Stormwind Keep, Varian’s anger hardened that judgment. The full shape of the treachery had yet to be weighed, and the roads beneath Lordaeron were already turning toward a second conflict.

storyNodes.title: Undercity falls to its traitors
storyNodes.narration: Beyond the battlefield, Varimathras and Grand Apothecary Putress turned against Sylvanas and seized Undercity. Its ruler had lost the halls beneath Lordaeron to a revolt within her own people. Later accounts name the two traitors, yet whether Sylvanas knew their design before Angrathar remains unresolved. With the city in other hands, the Horde’s answer would need to begin at its own gates.

storyNodes.title: The Horde turns back to Lordaeron
storyNodes.narration: Thrall called the Horde back to Lordaeron. Sylvanas, driven from her own city, sought to reclaim the halls and confront Varimathras’s forces. The capital had fallen to traitors, not to an open Scourge host, yet the plague had made that distinction bitterly contested. The counterattack turned from the northern front to a fight within Forsaken stone, while the Lich King still commanded the north.

storyNodes.title: Jaina carries a warning
storyNodes.narration: Jaina came to Orgrimmar with word that Varian would answer the Wrathgate by judging the Horde as one. She spoke with Thrall and Sylvanas while the Horde prepared to reclaim Undercity. The meeting restored no trust and promised no peace; it revealed how near the two factions had come to open war. Beyond the city walls, each account of Angrathar still carried a different wound.

storyNodes.title: The Alliance descends
storyNodes.narration: Varian led an Alliance force into Undercity by the sewers, with Jaina at his side. Their purpose was to reach Grand Apothecary Putress, whom they held responsible for the Wrathgate slaughter. Below Lordaeron, wet stone and iron conduits enclosed the column. The Alliance moved through a city already contested by the Horde; each assault sought its own answer to the betrayal.

storyNodes.title: The Horde re-enters the city
storyNodes.narration: From Undercity’s outer approaches, the Horde force advanced to reclaim its capital. Thrall and Sylvanas led the assault against Varimathras’s occupiers. The city had been built for its own people, yet its stairs and rising halls now narrowed into a battlefield. The Alliance had come by another way. Beneath Lordaeron, two separate offensives moved toward the same traitors.

storyNodes.title: A passage through the broken lift
storyNodes.narration: A destroyed elevator shaft divided the lower city from the heights. Thrall called on the elements of air to lift the Horde across the breach, and Sylvanas led them onward through the rising chambers. Behind them, the occupied halls had begun to fall. Ahead, the way climbed toward the Royal Quarter, where the dreadlord’s last defense waited in shadow.

storyNodes.title: The dreadlord in the Royal Quarter
storyNodes.narration: In the Royal Quarter, Varimathras turned the inner halls toward demonic allies and a final defense. Thrall and Sylvanas reached the dreadlord, bringing an end to his hold over Undercity. To the Horde, the city was retaken; yet the larger damage could not be named settled. Putress remained beyond Alliance hands, and Varian’s anger still pointed toward Thrall.

storyNodes.title: The Apothecarium’s evidence
storyNodes.narration: Through the Apothecarium’s low chambers, the Alliance assault reached Grand Apothecary Putress. His work lay exposed behind Undercity’s curved stone: among the evidence were human victims and signs of experiments. Their presence turned a pursuit for the gate’s poisoner into another wound between Forsaken and Alliance, one no victory over a single conspirator could heal.

storyNodes.title: The Alliance reaches Putress
storyNodes.narration: Putress’s defense failed before the Alliance force. The accused apothecary who had stood at the center of the Wrathgate betrayal no longer commanded the halls below Lordaeron. In another quarter, Thrall and Sylvanas had broken Varimathras’s hold. Each faction could name its target overcome, but the victories did not make their purposes one. Undercity had been retaken and searched, while trust remained lost.

storyNodes.title: Blades before the throne
storyNodes.narration: At the Royal Quarter, Varian found Thrall and sought an answer from the Warchief. Grief and anger pressed the Alliance king toward his rival, while Jaina remained close enough to see what was coming. The leaders’ blades drew near above Undercity’s black water. The Scourge had brought both armies north; beneath Lordaeron, they nearly turned upon one another.

storyNodes.title: Jaina opens the way out
storyNodes.narration: Jaina crossed the space between commanders. She froze the moment before steel could answer steel, then tore open a path for the Alliance to leave Undercity. Her magic spared the two forces an immediate battle, but it did not reconcile their leaders. The storm that had gathered at the gate now lived within the factions themselves, and the city’s dark waters held witness to a war barely averted.

storyNodes.title: No peace in the north
storyNodes.narration: The Horde held Undercity again; the Alliance had withdrawn; neither army could return to the old understanding. Thrall turned the eyes north once more: the Lich King still waited, and Icecrown had not fallen. The Wrathgate and the struggle beneath Lordaeron marked no true end to that war. A city had changed hands, one king was presumed lost, and trust remained divided between rival accounts.

storyNodes.title: A request at the port
storyNodes.narration: At Steamwheedle Port, Yeh’kinya asked a stranger to capture the spirits of Vale Screechers. He supplied a bramble, but his first words did not disclose the full purpose of the gathering. Beyond the desert harbor waited Feralas’s forested hills. A small request opened the search toward a power whose name had yet to reveal its danger.

storyNodes.title: Essence from the Vale
storyNodes.narration: From harbor dust, the seeker entered Feralas’s green shade and gathered the Vale Screechers’ spirits with the bramble. Their essence returned toward Yeh’kinya. The work had yielded what he sought without making his purpose plain. Within the forest’s living creatures, the stranger had found the beginning of a design that would reach far beyond the hills.

storyNodes.title: The prophecy of Mosh'aru
storyNodes.narration: Back in Tanaris, Yeh’kinya spoke of Hakkar and the prophecy of Mosh’aru. He asked for its tablets. In his telling, the gathered spirits belonged to a greater purpose, though the seeker had not yet learned all that he meant to do. The search turned toward written words that might explain the essence already placed in his keeping.

storyNodes.title: Two tablets, one promise
storyNodes.narration: Within Zul’Farrak’s sandstone halls, guardians held two tablets of Mosh’aru. The recovered prophecy described a means of containing an essence. The search had found the words Yeh’kinya wanted, but his whole purpose remained concealed. From the desert ruins, the tablets returned toward a plan whose promised safety could not yet be trusted.

storyNodes.title: The Ancient Egg in Jintha'Alor
storyNodes.narration: At Jintha’Alor, the Ancient Egg waited in a cave behind the high amphitheater. The seeker recovered it and returned toward Yeh’kinya with the vessel his plan required. Tablets and relic had come from distant places into one keeping. Their gathering brought the stranger nearer the rite he had described, while the full burden of that trust remained unknown.

storyNodes.title: The egg changes hands
storyNodes.narration: At the port, Yeh’kinya received the egg and the tablets. His next direction led to the Sunken Temple, where a rite would call forth Hakkar’s essence. From forest spirits and desert writings, the search had reached a drowned sanctuary. What had been gathered into his plan would now be used, and the stranger’s trust approached the danger hidden within it.

storyNodes.title: The Sanctum of the Fallen God
storyNodes.narration: Deep in the drowned temple, the seeker reached the Sanctum of the Fallen God. Atal’ai bloodrinkers stood among its threats. The tablets and Ancient Egg had brought Yeh’kinya’s design into the old halls. Beneath the temple’s dark waters, the rite began, drawing the scattered preparations toward the presence they had been meant to summon.

storyNodes.title: An avatar enters the world
storyNodes.narration: An avatar of Hakkar appeared, a skeletal wind serpent called into the Sunken Temple. The seeker fought and defeated that summoned presence. Hakkar’s later physical manifestation still lay beyond this encounter. Within the drowned sanctuary, the victory had reached an avatar and the essence the rite sought, leaving the greater danger outside the limits of the battle.

storyNodes.title: The egg stirs
storyNodes.narration: The avatar’s essence was placed within the Ancient Egg. Yeh’kinya promised to keep the vessel safe. Yet the egg stirred. The rite had reached its intended end without offering certainty that the danger was contained. Back at the desert port, the object carried a troubling life within it, and the seeker’s trust had begun to meet an unanswered warning.

storyNodes.title: Ironboot and the six tablets
storyNodes.narration: Prospector Ironboot sent the seeker after the remaining tablets of Mosh’aru. Beyond the first pair, other words survived that could change the meaning of Yeh’kinya’s plan. The search opened again. What had seemed a completed rite now depended upon a fuller reading of the prophecy, and upon knowledge its keeper had not placed before the stranger.

storyNodes.title: The third and fourth tablets
storyNodes.narration: In the Eastern Plaguelands, the search climbed to an old troll ziggurat. Two more tablets were recovered among its stones and carried back toward Ironboot. The prophecy’s scattered words had survived within another wounded country. Their recovery brought the inquiry nearer the meaning of the egg that had begun to stir in Yeh’kinya’s keeping.

storyNodes.title: The final pair in the mountain
storyNodes.narration: The final pair lay among the Smolderthorn trolls in Blackrock Spire. With their recovery, the six tablets could be read together. Ironboot would weigh what the fuller prophecy meant for the Ancient Egg. The search had crossed ruined places to gather words withheld from its first beginning; now those words could challenge the purpose Yeh’kinya had claimed.

storyNodes.title: Ironboot's warning
storyNodes.narration: Ironboot read a warning in the tablets: the egg might serve Hakkar’s rebirth within Zul’Gurub. The seeker had not witnessed that return, but the prospect changed the meaning of the temple rite. The avatar’s defeat could have supplied a later danger rather than ended it. Yeh’kinya’s promise of safe keeping now stood beneath a suspicion the stranger could no longer leave unanswered.

storyNodes.title: Yeh'kinya unmasked
storyNodes.narration: Confronted with the fuller prophecy, Yeh’kinya revealed that he intended to use the egg in Hakkar’s return. The promised containment had hidden another purpose. Tales of his escape spoke of a green wind serpent, but the disclosure itself was plain: the seeker had helped gather what he needed. The threatened rebirth remained beyond that confrontation, and aid against it had still to be sought.

storyNodes.title: The Hand of Rastakhan
storyNodes.narration: On Yojamba Isle, the seeker was directed to Molthor and asked to bring aid against Hakkar. The egg's gathering had ended in the revelation of a danger it was meant to serve. Molthor's appeal opened toward Zul'Gurub and a separate confrontation with the blood-god. The Ancient Egg's role in that later campaign remains unproven; the handoff carried the warning beyond the island.

storyNodes.title: Jin'do summons the Soulflayer
storyNodes.narration: On Yojamba Isle, Molthor's appeal pointed toward a threat beyond the tale of the Ancient Egg. During WoW Classic, Zul'Gurub's Gurubashi ruins became the setting of Jin'do the Hexxer's rite: he summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer into Azeroth. The Burning Crusade manual distinguishes this physical return from the avatar called in the Sunken Temple. No source gathered here proves that Yeh'kinya's egg enabled Jin'do's separate summoning.

storyNodes.title: The blood god banished
storyNodes.narration: After the Zul'Gurub confrontation, Blizzard's Burning Crusade Classic account records Hakkar banished to the plane from which he came. The physical Soulflayer's return had been turned back; the skeletal avatar called in the Sunken Temple remained a distinct episode. This summary leaves the individual victors unnamed and establishes no path from Yeh'kinya's Ancient Egg to Jin'do's rite. The immediate Classic peril ends here, while the egg's place in the later summoning remains unproven.
